value.Title: TIFT Presents - The Maids
value.Street: Barrie By The Bay Commercial Complex, 80 Bradford Street
value.Content:
Description:
Based on a true story, the darkly comic and unsettling The Maids tells an account of two sisters employed as servants in a wealthy household who engage in elaborate role-playing games, each taking turns as their superior, Madame. However, thanks to long-suppressed frustrations and desires, their private rituals intensify with devastating consequences. This celebrated drama is a provocative examination of social hierarchy and the masks people wear to survive in a world filled with inequality.

Show Times: Visit tift.ca

value.Title: Culture Days
value.Content:
Description:
Each year, the City of Barrie is proud to celebrate Culture Days, a Canada-wide celebration designed to catalyze and inspire public participation in the arts and culture. 

Culture Days programs invite the public to show appreciation for arts and culture in their own communities and nationwide. The Culture Days organization supports a Canada-wide network of arts, culture, and heritage organizers to facilitate free public events in their communities every year.

Running September 18 until October 4, 2026, Culture Days is Canada's largest cross-country celebration of arts, culture, and creativity.

Check back as September 18 approaches for a list of 2026 Culture Days programming as it's confirmed, and follow @creativebarrie on Instagram & Facebook for updates!

Click here for a full list of programming.

value.Title: Son of a Temperance - The South Simcoe Theatre
value.Street: The South Simcoe Theatre, 1 Hamilton Street
value.Content:
Description:
Son of a Temperance is a lively, heartfelt celebration of Cookstown’s past, unfolding inside the very walls where history was made – the old Temperance Hall, now home to the beloved South Simcoe Theatre.  As we mark our 60th Anniversary Season, this original play brings to life the spirited stories, community triumphs and colourful characters who shaped our building’s legacy. 

Set in 1878 Cookstown, this lively comedy follows the clash between the town’s zealous Templars and the proprietors of the local Temperance House, where rules are bent and secrets are brewed. Inspired by real local history, the play serves up fast-paced humour, small-town rivalries, and a toast to community mischief.

Recommended for ages 16 and up.

Show Times: September 18 - 20, 2026; Friday & Saturday: 7:30pm; Sunday: 2pm
Tickets: $25.00

value.Title: Pumpkin Mania
value.Content:
Description: 
Pumpkin Mania runs Saturdays, Sundays, and Holiday Mondays. Soak up the fresh country air and enjoy a full day at Ranchland with over 25 activities included in admission, plus a Pick-Your-Own (PYO) free pumpkin, any size, any colour.

Families can explore the Petting Zoo, Corn Maze, Tractor Rides, the Buckaroo Bouncer, and many more attractions that will keep everyone entertained for hours. Ranchland’s 25+ self-guided and staff-led activities are all included with admission, along with the PYO pumpkin experience.

Pumpkin Mania Games take place every half hour and feature Pumpkin Tosses, Slam Dunk Pumpkin challenges, Pumpkin Bowling, Seed Spitting, and the always-popular Pumpkin Pie Eating Contests. Winners earn a Pumpkin Prize Token, redeemable at the Pumpkin Hut for treats like candy, popcorn, and fun prizes. Guests can also watch for Peek-A-Boo Pumpkins hidden around the ranch, find one and win a special prize at the Pumpkin Hut.

Visitors can add a little extra to their day with Animal Feed ($5/bag), Pony Rides ($10/ride), Corn Cannon shots ($5 for 8), additional pumpkins (one is included per admission), the Cookhouse (open daily), and the Mercantile Gift Shop (open daily).

Come make unforgettable fall-time memories at Rounds Ranch, a family-run farm filled with outdoor adventure and seasonal fun.

value.Title: Reimagine History at Fort Willow
value.Description:
Join the Historic Military Establishment of Upper Canada for a weekend garrison at Historic Fort Willow. The public is invited to explore the fort in a historical context and witness what life was like for soldiers during the War of 1812.

Throughout the weekend, visitors can observe live demonstrations including:

- Musket and cannon firing drills
- War of 1812 military drills
- Historical fashion presentations

In addition, on Friday, May 30, students from St. Joseph’s Catholic High School will be on-site conducting an archaeological dig. Visitors are welcome to stop by, observe the excavation, and chat with students about their discoveries.
value.Content:
Description:
Step back in time and discover the stories, people and places that shaped the region at Fort Willow Conservation Area.

On September 19, retired history teacher Joe Cinnani will bring history to life through artifacts, photographs, guided tours and vivid storytelling. Imagine what life was like for the people who travelled through Fort Willow and the surrounding area throughout history, and uncover the stories behind this important historic site.

Visit Fort Willow Conservation Area during Doors Open Simcoe County on Saturday, September 19, for a fascinating journey through centuries of local history.

Date: Saturday, September 19, 2026
Time: 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
Location: Fort Willow Conservation Area, 2714 Grenfel Road, Utopia
Admission: Free; parking fees waived
Registration: No registration required

value.Title: Hearth to Table: Dinner in 1648 at Sainte-Marie among the Hurons
value.Street: Sainte-Marie among the Hurons, 16164 Highway 12 East
value.Content:
Description:
Savour 17th-century-inspired gourmet dishes by candlelight right on the grounds of historic Sainte-Marie. Hearth to Table invites guests to gather around a harvest table inside the chapel of the reconstructed Jesuit mission and enjoy a delicious, multi-course meal featuring historic seasonal ingredients. Start each course with an introduction from a costumed interpreter specializing in 17th-century cooking.

Learn to appreciate the many challenges and intricacies – from basic technology to limited vegetable options – of preparing an epicurean French-style meal in this era. Then enjoy your taste of history! June Menu: Indigenous June Dinner Three Sisters Pottage A comforting pottage celebrating the Three Sisters: corn, beans, and squash, slow‑simmered into a nourishing stew.

Served alongside freshly made fry bread Roasted Squash & Sunflower Seeds: Sweet roasted squash paired with toasted sunflower seeds, highlighting ingredients central to Haudenosaunee agricultural tradition. Maple-Brined Venison: Tender venison infused with a delicate maple brine, then roasted to bring out deep woodland flavours. Haudenosaunee-Inspired Strawberry Bread: A lightly sweet bread made with fresh strawberries and baked in a simple, traditional style. Wine and beer pairings available at an additional cost.

Select Saturdays: May 30, June 27, July 25, August 22, September 19, October 10
Cost: $95.40

value.Title: TIFT Presents - Don't Touch The Art
value.Street: Barrie By The Bay Commercial Complex, 80 Bradford Street
value.Content:
Description:

In an immersive experience devised and curated by Griffin Hewitt, Don't Touch the Art transforms a large building into a living gallery of performance where multiple works, both new and TIFT favourites, unfold simultaneously across rooms, hallways, and hidden corners. Each encounter is designed to be a surprise, and every choice to enter, remain or move on to find a different installation will shape a unique self-directed journey for each patron.

No two experiences are exactly alike: the combination of works, encounters, and pathways available on any given evening may also differ, creating new possibilities for every return visit. Don't Touch the Art blurs the boundaries between exhibition, performance, and exploration, inviting audiences to become active participants in a theatrical experience unlike any other.

 

Show Times & Admission: Visit tift.ca

 

Make It More Than a Night at the Theatre

Make your Don’t Touch the Art experience a little bigger. Arrive early for dinner at a local Barrie restaurant, wander Downtown Barrie and take in the waterfront before stepping into a theatre experience where you choose your own path. Stay the night and turn an evening at the theatre into a full Barrie getaway.

value.Title: Doors Open Barrie
value.Content:
Description:
Doors Open Barrie showcases the history and architecture of our city and celebrates the places that make it special. Each year, communities across Ontario dedicate a day for local sites of interest to be opened to the public for free tours. Doors Open Barrie will take place on Saturday, September 26, 2026. 

Doors Open is an Ontario Heritage Trust program that invites communities across the province to open the doors, gates and courtyards of their unique and most fascinating cultural sites so residents and visitors can see inside! It’s a chance to explore Ontario’s heritage treasures at free public events across the province.

It provides unique opportunities to explore and enjoy some of the most interesting places in Ontario cities, towns and villages. Step inside local landmarks and heritage sites. and creative spaces to explore Barrie's stories.

BARRIE'S HIDDEN PAST - HERITAGE WALKING TOUR

A Heritage Walking Tour: Discover Barrie’s rich and surprising history on this guided walking tour. 

We’ll explore landmarks like the charming old farmhouse, the Tourism Barrie building, the historic General John Hayter Southshore Centre and Allandale GO Station. Learn about the days when ice was harvested from Lake Simcoe, hear whispers of a sunken ship, and hear about the legend of Kempenfelt Kelly, our very own lake monster. It’s a short walk packed with stories that bring Barrie’s shoreline to life!

Register Here

Please note: Space is limited, and completing this form does not guarantee a spot. Tourism Barrie will confirm availability by email using the email address you provided during registration. To help us reserve the correct number of spaces, please ensure you include the full names of all participants you are registering.

value.Title: Barrie Historical Archive presents "Amoi"
value.Street: The Five Points Theatre, 1 Dunlop Street West
value.Content:
Description:
1859. A British officer and his Chinese wife defy convention, shocking two empires. This is the remarkable story of Amy 'Amoi' Bird, lady of Sans Souci, an unlikely pioneer, who forged a life of resilience and strength in Barrie.

The Barrie Historical Archive presents an original documentary film, 'Amoi'. In Barrie's long and fascinating history, one unique story stands out. It began in China with a forbidden marriage. In 1859, British officer Shearman Bird risked everything when he wed Amoi Chun, a Chinese woman. From war torn China to rural England, they searched for a safe haven to raise their children and found that place in Barrie.

A family tragedy changed everything, and Amoi became the rock of her family and a beloved Barrie citizen. Traces of this remarkable time can still be seen in 'Sans Souci, the delightful home that Shearman built for his family. Please join us as we proudly present the premiere showing of a Barrie story like no other.

Show Times: 7:00pm
Admission: $29.50

value.Title: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
value.Description: Every child matters. On the National Day of Truth and Reconciliation at Sainte-Marie among the Hurons, we invite you to join us for a journey of self-reflection.  Begin by honoring the survivors of residential schools in a solemn ceremony.  As we observe this day of contemplation and remembrance, our historical interpreters will shift their focus towards the journey of truth and reconciliation, fostering opportunities for genuine listening and learning.  In the spirit of education and awareness, we encourage you to engage with Indigenous speakers and cultural specialists, as we collectively navigate the path to truth and reconciliation.
value.Street: Sainte-Marie among the Hurons, 16164 Highway 12 East
value.Content:
Description:
Join us at Sainte-Marie among the Hurons for the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, a day dedicated to learning, reflection, and remembrance. Explore the history and lasting impacts of residential schools with survivor testimonials, guided experiences, guest speakers, traditional foodways, and film screenings.

Participate in meaningful ceremonies throughout the day, including a Sunrise Ceremony, Survivor Flag Raising, and Smudge Ceremony. Admission is free, and programming runs from 6 a.m. to 4 p.m.

value.Title: Hearth to Table: Dinner in 1648 at Sainte-Marie among the Hurons
value.Street: Sainte-Marie among the Hurons, 16164 Highway 12 East
value.Content:
Description:
Savour 17th-century-inspired gourmet dishes by candlelight right on the grounds of historic Sainte-Marie. Hearth to Table invites guests to gather around a harvest table inside the chapel of the reconstructed Jesuit mission and enjoy a delicious, multi-course meal featuring historic seasonal ingredients. Start each course with an introduction from a costumed interpreter specializing in 17th-century cooking.

Learn to appreciate the many challenges and intricacies – from basic technology to limited vegetable options – of preparing an epicurean French-style meal in this era. Then enjoy your taste of history! June Menu: Indigenous June Dinner Three Sisters Pottage A comforting pottage celebrating the Three Sisters: corn, beans, and squash, slow‑simmered into a nourishing stew.

Served alongside freshly made fry bread Roasted Squash & Sunflower Seeds: Sweet roasted squash paired with toasted sunflower seeds, highlighting ingredients central to Haudenosaunee agricultural tradition. Maple-Brined Venison: Tender venison infused with a delicate maple brine, then roasted to bring out deep woodland flavours. Haudenosaunee-Inspired Strawberry Bread: A lightly sweet bread made with fresh strawberries and baked in a simple, traditional style. Wine and beer pairings available at an additional cost.

value.Title: Barrie Concerts Presents "Chamber Scenes"
value.Content:
Description:
The Millwood Trio unites three of Canada’s most distinguished musicians, whose artistic paths have intertwined for nearly thirty years. Violinist Jasper Wood, pianist Gregory Millar, and clarinetist Michael Westwood bring together decades of experience, profound musical insight, and a finely tuned collaborative instinct, creating an ensemble voice that is at once luminous, sensitive, and compelling.

Their performances combine clarity, warmth, and expressive depth, drawing audiences into a richly textured chamber-music experience. Over decades of collaboration, the trio has cultivated a rare musical chemistry, allowing them to approach the repertoire for violin, clarinet, and piano with remarkable precision, interpretive depth, and expressive nuance.

Their programs encompass classical masterpieces, 20th-century innovations, and contemporary works, each brought to life with keen attention to detail, dynamic contrast, and the subtle interplay that arises from nearly thirty years of shared artistry.

Long Live made their official debut with a sold out show at the Hudson Village Theatre in January.

Featuring Noelle Hannibal (vocals, guitar) Ian Baird (keys, backing vocals), Lewis Orenstein (bass), Robert Flis (guitar) and Gopal D (drums). Start preparing your outfits and making your friendship bracelets! We can't wait to see you!

value.Title: Huronia Symphony Orchestra Presents 'Sixty Years In Motion'
value.Street: Collier Street United Church, 112 Collier Street
value.Content:
Description:
We open the season celebrating 60 years of the Huronia Symphony, an extraordinary community orchestra shaped by the musicians who bring it to life.

Hear our own concertmaster perform the much beloved Bruch’s Violin Concerto No. 1, a work of lyric warmth and expressive beauty. It speaks with an intimate voice that feels both personal and deeply rooted in the orchestra's sound.

In Sibelius' Symphony No. 2, that voice expands outward into something large, music that gathers momentum, builds in strength, and moves toward a powerful sense of shared arrival.

Together, these works reflect how a musical community is shaped over time, through individual voices, collective energy, and the way musicians listen, respond, and support each other.

value.Title: First Light
value.Description:
Celebrating 25 years of holiday magic
Now in its 25th year, Sainte-Marie’s First Light is an award-winning, must-see holiday event with a great lineup of family activities and live musical performances, all amidst the spectacular glow of thousands of candles.  
This year, you’re visiting two candlelit attractions for the price of one: Sainte-Marie among the Hurons and Martyrs’ Shrine!
Start your holiday shopping at our extensive artisan market. Enjoy activities for kids at both Sainte-Marie and the Martyrs’ Shrine. See historical demonstrations including blacksmithing. Take part in Sunday night mass. Enjoy a delicious holiday meal, and much more!
There’s a reason this event is an annual tradition for many. Come and experience a little holiday magic! 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The anniversary edition of First Light will feature all the classic elements of this beloved event… plus a few fun new twists!
•	Wander through candlelit paths and historic buildings
•	Watch live music including celtic harp in the church and hand-drumming in the longhouse
•	Start your holiday shopping at our extensive artisan market featuring 50+ local vendors
•	Enjoy activities for kids at both attractions
•	See historical demonstrations including blacksmithing and candlemaking
•	Explore a unique activity each night, including fireworks on Thursdays
•	Book a delicious holiday meal at Restaurant Sainte-Marie, including a chance to dine in your own personal snow globe
•	NEW: Join a candlelit choir on Fridays!
•	NEW: Help to light candles and see Sainte-Marie all lit up, before the crowds, in a new Behind-the-scenes experience!
•	and much more!
There’s a reason this event is an annual tradition for many. Come and experience a little holiday magic! 
__________________________________________________________________________
Add-ons:
First Light Behind the Scenes Experience
Access First Light before doors officially open!
From 4:30 to 5:30 p.m., you’ll help light the lanterns that transform Sainte-Marie into a candlelit winter wonderland, then settle into a cozy longhouse to sip warm spiced apple cider while listening to First Nations stories.
Then, your costumed guide will escort you to Restaurant Sainte-Marie for dinner. Choose classic indoor dining, or elevate your evening with a three-course meal served in your own private snow globe under the stars.
It’s an unforgettable way to begin your First Light journey!
 
Friday Candlelight Chorus
Add a spark of joy to your First Light experience by joining a one-night candlelight choir led by Choir Revolution’s Brett Caswell! No singing experience or skill needed, just bring your voice and your spirit. From 5 to 6:30 p.m. you’ll learn one of three simple parts (high, mid, low) for the song “Put a Little Love in Your Heart” from Scrooged in our indoor theatre with fellow music lovers. Then at 6:45 p.m. you’ll perform outside the Church of Saint Joseph on the historic site, surrounded by lanterns, with each chorister holding their own candle. After your performance, soak in the magic of this beloved holiday celebration. Come for the lights, stay for the harmony, and leave with a little more love in your heart.
value.Street: Sainte-Marie among the Hurons, 16164 Highway 12 East
value.Content:
Description:
Wander through candlelit paths and discover a historical winter wonderland like no other. Take in live musical performances, watch blacksmithing demonstrations, listen to stories in the longhouse, and so much more. Each night of the week includes a special activity or feature!

Enjoy a holiday buffet inside Restaurant Sainte-Marie’s cozy dining room, get takeout on the patio, or elevate your dining experience by booking your own personal snow globe on the grounds of historic Sainte-Marie. Plus, get snacks and hot chocolate right on the historic site.

Get started on your holiday shopping! Explore one of the region’s most extensive and impressive holiday artisan markets with more than 50 local vendors selling only handmade goods, from socks to soaps and sweet treats. Warm up as you explore booths in our indoor museum and Brebeuf Centre.

Cost of admission: to both Sainte-Marie and the Martyrs’ Shrine is $15 per person, tax included. Walk-ins welcome!

  • Children 5 & under are free
  • First Nations, Métis and Inuit people are eligible for free entry with a valid ID
  • Season passes are valid for this event
  • Members of the Canadian Armed Forces get free admission with a valid ID
  • A person accompanying a paying guest with a disability is eligible for free admission

Activities:

  • Holiday glow: Wander through a stunning display of seasonal lights.
  • Santa and holiday craft: Bring the family and enjoy a visit with Saint-Nicholas, perfect for young guests and the young at heart. Complete your visit with a fun holiday craft!
  • Live music in the church: Enjoy musical performances inside the gorgeous Martyrs’ Shrine church, all decorated for Christmas. On Saturdays and Sundays, listen to the a capella choir Shrine Schola.
  • Light a candle: Pause for reflection and light a special candle in the votary, a simple yet meaningful gesture of hope, remembrance, or prayer.
  • Browse the gift shop: Warm up and browse a thoughtful selection of gifts, keepsakes, and seasonal items in the gift shop, ideal for holiday giving.
  • Shop vendors: Shop local vendors downstairs in the Martyrs’ Shrine church.
  • Mass on Sundays: Attend Sunday evening Mass with live choral music at 7:30 p.m. during First Light and mark the beginning of the Advent season in community.

value.Title: Georgian Music Presents "Leaves of an Unwritten Diary"
value.Street: Bethel Community Church, 128 St. Vincent Street
value.Content:
Description:
This concert is part of the Sunday Georgian Music series.

Celebrating their 40th anniversary, the Penderecki String Quartet began their career as winners of the Penderecki Prize at the National Chamber Music Competition in Łódz, Poland in 1986. Now based in Waterloo, Ontario, where they have been Quartet-in-Residence at Wilfrid Laurier University since 1991, the Penderecki String Quartet has become one of the most celebrated chamber ensembles of their generation.

The four Penderecki musicians (now originating from Poland, Canada, and USA) bring their varied yet collective experience to create performances that demonstrate their “remarkable range of technical excellence and emotional sweep” (Toronto Globe and Mail).

value.Title: Huronia Symphony Orchestra Presents 'Of Love Remembered'
value.Street: Collier Street United Church, 112 Collier Street
value.Content:
Description:
Love in its most intimate and reflective form, not as declaration, but as memory and transformation.

Schubert’s Rosamunde Overture opens a world of lyric warmth and quiet Romantic beauty, where emotional openness exists before it is ever defined. Wagner’s Siegfried Idyll turns inward, offering music of private devotion. Brahms’ Third Symphony completes the journey, where emotion is no longer spoken directly, but absorbed into structure and memory.

Together, these works reveal how love can persist, not in presence, but in remembrance.

Show Time: 3:30pm - 5:30pm

value.Title: The Drawer Boy - The South Simcoe Theatre
value.Street: The South Simcoe Theatre, 1 Hamilton Street
value.Content:
Description:
An actor arrives at a remote Ontario farm to research a play and meets Angus and Morgan, lifelong friends and World War II veterans living quietly together. As memories surface, their shared past reveals how storytelling, loyalty, and friendship can both protect and transform. The Drawer Boy, by celebrated Canadian playwright Michael Healey, is the winner of the 1999 Governor General’s Literary Award for English-Language Drama; a Dora Mavor Moore Award for Outstanding New Play; and the Floyd S. Chalmers Canadian Play Award for outstanding contribution to Canadian playwriting.

Recommended for ages 16 and up.

Show Times: February 19 - March 7, 2027; Fridays & Saturdays: 7:30pm; Sundays: 2pm
Tickets: $30.00

value.Title: Barrie Concerts Presents "Musical Illusions"
value.Content:
Description:
Sheng Cai & Beverly Wang form a dynamic piano–oboe duo uniting two internationally acclaimed Canadian artists. Combining virtuosity, tonal beauty, and thoughtful programming, they present chamber music performances of exceptional depth, elegance, and expressive range.

New World Piano/Oboe Duo (Cai & Wang) reimagines the oboe–piano repertoire from Europe and the Americas, blending core works with rare and contemporary voices. With performances across Canada, the U.S., and Mexico in the 2026–27 season, the duo brings fresh energy, virtuosity, and bold programming to three centuries of music.

value.Title: Georgian Music Presents "Soul of Venezuela"
value.Street: Bethel Community Church, 128 St. Vincent Street
value.Content:
Description:
This concert is part of the Sunday Georgian Music series.

No strangers to performing with each other, Eliana and Jeremy have been performing together in various configurations for over 15 years, including Eliana’s last three albums which earned them two US Independent Music Awards for Best World Music Album and Best World Music Producer in New York, and a Canadian Folk Music Award for Best World Music Album.

Eliana’s extraordinary vocal prowess is on full display in this duo setting, showcasing the vocal chops that have been captivating audiences around the world for years. At the hands of Jeremy Ledbetter, the piano roars, whispers, cries, and is transformed into a Venezuelan cuatro, or an «arpa llanera», in a mesmerizing display of versatility. On stage, Eliana and Jeremy open a window into their lives, creating a display of their experiences together through music, taking advantage of their personal connection to bring their songs and stories to life.

value.Title: TIFT Presents - M. Butterfly
value.Street: Site-specific location in Barrie to be announced
value.Content:
Description:

The gripping and thought-provoking drama, inspired by true events, blends political intrigue, romance, and questions of identity as it follows a French diplomat who becomes entangled in a decades-long relationship with a mysterious Chinese opera performer. As assumptions, fantasies and realities collide, long-held perceptions are challenged with disastrous consequences.
